blogs.title: How LongRoPE Pushes LLM Memory Past 2 Million Tokens
blogs.description: An accessible overview of the paper’s biggest achievement: extending large language models from typical 4k–128k context windows all the way to 2,048k tokens. The post would explain why long context matters, what breaks when models read beyond their trained limits, and how LongRoPE makes ultra-long reading possible with only minor changes to positional embeddings.

blogs.title: Why LLMs Forget in Long Conversations—and the Positional Embedding Fix Behind LongRoPE
blogs.description: A beginner-friendly deep dive into RoPE positional embeddings and why context extension is so hard. The post would explain the paper’s key insight that not all token positions and RoPE dimensions should be stretched equally, showing how ‘non-uniform interpolation’ helps models preserve important positional information instead of collapsing under very long inputs.

blogs.title: From 4K to 2M Without Massive Retraining: The Smart Scaling Strategy of LongRoPE
blogs.description: This post would focus on LongRoPE’s progressive extension recipe: first extending a model to 256k, then using a second interpolation step to reach 2048k. It would highlight why this staged approach is cheaper and more practical than directly training on million-token documents, making the paper especially interesting for engineers working with limited compute.

blogs.title: Search, Don’t Guess: How Evolutionary Optimization Helps LongRoPE Find Better Context Windows
blogs.description: A post centered on the paper’s search algorithm. Instead of hand-designing how positional scaling should work, LongRoPE uses an evolutionary search to discover better scaling factors across dimensions and token positions. The article would explain this idea in plain language and show why automated search beats one-size-fits-all heuristics like standard linear interpolation.

blogs.title: Can an LLM Really Read a Million Tokens? What LongRoPE’s Benchmarks Actually Show
blogs.description: A results-focused blog post covering the experiments behind the hype. It would translate perplexity, passkey retrieval, and short-context benchmark scores into plain English, helping readers understand what it means for a model to keep over 90% retrieval accuracy at extreme lengths while still performing well on normal tasks.
